title: I built a free, open-source asset studio for making games with coding agents. It's very experimental. What's missing for your game?
author: shaco_player
selftext:
Video shows the whole flow. Short version: Glob is a desktop app where you make the art for your game, and your coding agent (Claude Code, for example) then pulls the finished files into the game.



What you can do with it right now:



\- Generate 2D art: characters, items, environments, UI and VFX

\- Keep a consistent style with reference images that get sent with every generation, for the whole project or just one folder

\- Turn images into 3D models, with poly count and export to OBJ, STL or USDZ

\- Rig 3D models and add animations from a library

\- Make sound effects, voices and music, then trim them and check that they loop

\- Turn any image into square, transparent inventory icons

\- Build level kits: picture a level, get its props on one sheet, and Glob cuts out and names each prop for you

\- Cut sprite sheets into parts, or render sprite sheets from a 3D model

\- Build a rough playable prototype from your art to test whether the idea is fun

\- Import an existing Godot, Unity or Unreal project, or any folder of art



What to know before trying it:



\- It's free and open source (MIT), but the AI generators are not. You connect your own accounts and pay them directly. I don't add any markup or subscription.

\- Everything is generated through online services for now. You can't run image or 3D generators on your own PC yet, though it should be possible to add that later.

\- It's built around Claude. Codex might work, but I don't have it, so I haven't tested it.

\- It's very experimental, so expect bugs. Pull requests are welcome.



Which of these would you actually use, and what's missing for your game?



GitHub: [https://github.com/SoulNassim/Glob-Game-Forge](https://github.com/SoulNassim/Glob-Game-Forge)

Try it in your browser, no keys needed: [https://soulnassim.github.io/Glob-Game-Forge/demo/](https://soulnassim.github.io/Glob-Game-Forge/demo/)

(Release builds are kinda broken sometimes so id suggest asking your agent to just install it)
